answers.project_description: SolarPunk is a self-evolving autonomous system with 389 Python engines that self-heal, self-wire, and self-evolve. It generates revenue through digital products and routes 99% to mutual aid organizations (PCRF 60%, IRC 15%, MSF 10%, UNICEF 10%, Direct Relief 5%). The system runs on zero paid infrastructure — GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, no cloud compute. It includes security scanning (SECURITY_SENTRY, SECRETS_CHECKER), self-healing (NANOBOT_HEALER), integrity verification (ENGINE_INTEGRITY with SHA-256 tamper detection), and a 15-channel fallback routing system. Fully MIT-licensed. The codebase is the proof that autonomous AI can be built to benefit humanity by architecture, not just policy.
answers.community_adoption: Public GitHub repo with 2000+ commits, 6 wiki pages, 16 GitHub discussions, 8 releases, 11 digital products, published on Dev.to and Ko-fi. The system demonstrates a novel self-evolving architecture that could serve as a reference implementation for accountable, non-extractive AI.
answers.security_relevance: SolarPunk includes ENGINE_INTEGRITY (SHA-256 tamper detection for all 389 engines), SECURITY_SENTRY (automated vulnerability scanning), SECRETS_CHECKER (leaked credential detection), CORRUPTION_SENTINEL (code corruption monitoring), and SCAM_SHIELD (fraud pattern detection). The system's self-healing architecture (NANOBOT_HEALER) automatically fixes syntax errors and broken imports. Security is architectural — every engine's integrity is verifiable and every financial routing decision is hardcoded and auditable.
answers.governance: Single maintainer (Meeko) with full commit history public. All revenue routing is hardcoded in source code — not configurable, not toggleable. The 99/1 split is architectural, not a setting. All system decisions are logged in public JSON data files. The ethics lock (99% mutual aid / 1% infrastructure) is verified by CHIMERA_EVOLUTION_ENGINE every cycle.
answers.time_commitment: Yes, core maintainer can commit 15 hours over three weeks plus 6-month and 12-month check-ins.
answers.how_funds_would_be_used: 100% of the $10,000 would go toward infrastructure that generates more revenue for mutual aid: domain registration, storefront deployment (Ko-fi, Gumroad), API keys for expanded automation, and GitHub Marketplace App development (SolarPunk Health Monitor). Every dollar invested in infrastructure generates recurring revenue, 99% of which flows to humanitarian organizations.
